notes.mapStructure:
Map STRUCTURE — the roads and plain rings a player reads to plan a run
(#45, Sunna's ruling: 3:1 on each glyph's identifying boundary against each
adjacent rendered colour). --line-soft's atmospheric value measures 1.93
(edge vs field) / 1.72 (ring vs its own fill) from rendered pixels — below
every defensible floor — but its 27 other consumers are text-adjacent soft
lines that keep the atmospheric look ("atmospheric elsewhere"). So the map
graph rides its own token: #7a6b54 clears both adjacencies with margin
(rendered 3.78 vs field, 3.36 worst adjacency) while staying the visibly
dimmer sibling of high contrast's 4.19 — two settings, two looks.
Evidence: tools/contrast-audit.mjs --profile hi-contrast-off;
the former atmospheric map-structure proposal (R2; removed 2026-10-11, see git history).
notes.resHp:
The HP resource fill — the approved hybrid's owner pixel (2026-08-13,
claude-family falk-family hybrid-confirmation, F1-resource-health.png),
minted as its OWN token so the accent themes keep owning the palette
(cb-safe swaps it below). Before this token the hp row wore var(--blood)
and the conflict was recorded, not resolved: token vs owner hex. Now both
hold — the value is the owner's, the swap is the theme's. --blood keeps
its 16 other consumers (map rings, danger buttons, enemy hpbars) and is
NOT this token.
notes.bleed:
THE KEYWORD TINT CARD TEXT USES, and it is a token because it is a fact
about a WORD, not about a container. It had no token, so the one palette
that wanted a different answer had nowhere to put it and put it in a
SELECTOR instead (`body.cb-safe .card .ctext .st-bleed`, deleted below).
When the five mark rules re-keyed `.card .ctext` → `.ctext` so the Smith
preview could wear them too, every token-based rule came through for free
and that one hardcoded hex stayed behind on the old container — so under
Colorblind-friendly the SAME WORD read reddish-purple on a card face and
vermillion in the preview. The hex was the reason it could not follow.
Derived from --ember, not restated: in the default palette Bleed wears the
ember hue TODAY, and that is a derivation, not a copy — one home for the
value. Colorblind-friendly overrides it once, below, which is the only
place the two diverge.
OPEN, AND FREJA'S, NOT MINE: whether the DEFAULT palette should diverge
too. It does not today — a Bleed keyword and a number the upgrade made
WORSE both render rgb(201,80,46) on every screen, one hue doing two jobs
on one line. Colorblind-friendly already answers that question `yes`.
notes.danger: The kit's danger tint (the kit page's rgba(212, 98, 46)); nothing in base.css named it, so every `.danger` weight read an unset variable.

notes.mapStructure: unchanged shipped value — hi-contrast map keeps its exact look

notes.resHp: the hp fill keeps tracking the danger hue (Okabe-Ito vermillion)
notes.danger: danger buttons track the same vermillion as --blood
notes.bleed:
Okabe-Ito reddish-purple — the SAME VALUE this palette already shipped,
moved out of a selector and into the token block where a palette decision
belongs. It now reaches card text wherever card text is drawn, which is
the whole change: the card face is byte-identical and the Smith
upgrade preview stops calling a keyword by the danger hue.
